lines.en: : Okay...can someone explain to me what’s going on here?
: I was under the impression that I was going to the movies with Ami.
: We are going to the movies! I just need to kick Ayane’s butt in a cooking competition first!
: Oh, please! As if I’d let you win a competition as important as this!
: This might be the only chance I ever get to directly compete against you for Sensei's heart! I will not let you take this from me!
: Sensei doesn’t want your bubble wrap empire, Ayane!
: Neither do I so that's just one more thing we have in common!
So, here we are...The ultimate showdown between Ami and Ayane- two [teenage]girls giving all they have to impress three of us (But mostly me) with their cooking.
I'm a little worried about giving Ayane access to so many knives during a battle in which my love is the prize...but I figure I’ll be able to step in if she does decide to get all...’Ayane.’
: Um...thank you again...for inviting me over...
: I’m sorry to...intrude like this...
: It's fine. Make yourself at home.
: And what is this? When did you two start warming up to one another? Why are so many strange things happening today?
: U-Umm...Sensei...has been coming to the bar I work at recently and...
: He’s been helping me...get more comfortable around other people...
: Is that so?...
: I didn’t realize he was actually capable of instructing anyone in ways that don't directly benefit him.
: Everyone benefits from a more talkative Sana. She is a welcome investment of my time.
: Sana, blink twice if you are being forced to comply against your will.
: I'm...not a hostage! Sensei has...actually helped a lot!
: I’ve only cried a couple times so far!
: Was telling her that part really necessary?
: So...because you’ve only cried a couple times, you think he’s doing a good job?
: See? Now she's just going to use that against us and you're never going to learn how to talk.
: I'm sorry...I...I...
: Sana, if you really want help when it comes to communicating, let me handle it. I can guarantee you I'll be of more assistance than him.
: We're trying to teach her how to talk to other people, not how to make them feel insignificant and unwelcome.
: I...think Sensei...is doing a good job...and um...I think...I'm going to stay...with him...
: You will regret this decision, but it is yours to make.
: Did...um...something happen between you two?...
: You seem...a little different outside of school...
: Don’t mind them, Sana! Those two are never going to get along. Me and Ayane have already accepted it.
Ami calls out from the kitchen and sums up the relationship between Maya and me pretty perfectly.
I don’t know if I’d go as far as saying that we’ll never get along, though...
Maya will have to warm up to me some day, right?
Right?
: How much longer do we need to wait until this competition actually begins? I'm starving and I envisioned myself with several buckets full of popcorn by now.
: You're gonna have to ask Ayane. She's the one who's supposed to be going-
: Silence! And fear no more, Maya! For the first course of several unbelievable courses is about to be served...
: We’ll be starting today off light and indulging in our wonderful culture with a staple of nearly every Japanese dish...rice.
: While it may not be the most exciting food item you will be eating today, it's important to remember that good rice can elevate a dish to unbelievable levels!
: And even though it may seem simple, there are countless different ways to use it and even more ways to-
: I'm sorry, is the monologue part of the dish? Or am I allowed to eat now?
: You may eat! But please remember to like, comment, and subscribe if you enjoy it!
: Subscribe to...rice?...
: This seems like a lot of rice, Ayane. I don't really think any of us want to fill up on-
: Seconds, please.
: ...What?
Ayane’s rice is...well, rice.
It’s cooked properly and not seasoned in any way.
It’s just...a typical side dish you'd receive at a restaurant alongside miso soup.
That said, I couldn't really find any issues with it either. So I guess this sort of...simplistic form of cooking is in line with how Ayane likes to do things.
: Hi, everyone! Did you all enjoy Ayane's first dish? Or do you think it was super boring and that she should get locked inside of a shed somewhere?
: Hey! You can’t ask questions like that in the middle of the competition! It’s unfair!
: Sensei! Deduct points from her score!
: Please ignore the loud noises coming from the kitchen. Our ice machine broke and has been making a strange whining sound all morning.
: Ami! You know I hate it when you compare me to industrial appliances!
: Anyway! Please enjoy my version of Ayane’s super boring dish but with an extra special ingredient! Thank you very much for your time and remember to vote Ami!
: What?...
: Why are you both looking at me?
: We want to watch how you eat.
: I’m...also curious...
: I...don’t know...
: It’s just...kind of impressive, don’t you th-
: Seconds, please.
: Wha-
: We looked away for too long...
: It...was only a couple seconds...
: I honestly don't understand what you two are so riled up about. I'm just doing the same thing I always do.
: You are...always like this?...
: Just leave it alone, Sana. She's a monster...
Ami’s rice is...also rice.
However, just like she hinted at, there’s an extra special ingredient in it.
And that ingredient?...
Is love.
Just kidding. It’s salt.
Ami must have salted the rice before bringing it to us, which I greatly appreciate since I put salt on virtually everything.
And just like that, we have our first example of her directly catering to my tastes without thinking about what the other judges will think.
: So...what do you think, Sensei?...Which one was better?...
: Ami, without a doubt.
: Ayane’s rice was probably cooked a little better. But without any seasoning, I just can't say I'd choose it over Ami's.
: Sensei! You know that salt is bad for your heart, don't you? For the sake of your health, I think you should lay off.
: How do you expect to raise our children with your sodium levels through the roof?
: Stop trying to raise a family with my [uncle]!
: No!
: Anyway...I think I liked...Ayane’s more...
: I’m also going to choose Ayane for this round.
: I didn’t particularly favor either dish. I just don’t want to vote for the same person he does.
: Maya! That’s not how this works!
: I am an unbiased judge. Please continue on with the competition.
: So! Now that I've already won the first round, I’ll be counting on you guys to support my love- err...food at least one more time to lock in a victory for me!
: For the main course, we have a-
: Wait...Sana? What’s wrong?
: What happened? Did I do something wrong?
: Uhh...
: I’m surprised you haven’t heard about this story, Ayane.
: Story? What story?
: Sana has a traumatic experience when it comes to spaghetti.
: What? How does that even happen?
: I...can't do this...
: It’s a long story.
: Uhh...
: I’m just going to eat now.
Despite Sana’s disposition toward the dish, Ayane’s pasta is quite nice.
I'm not sure if it's something that I could eat every day. But it's definitely something I wouldn't mind ordering again if this were a restaurant.
I think it's pretty safe to say Ayane has already lost one voter for this round, though...
: Are you okay?
: I’ll be fine...
: I can’t believe this is a sentence I am about to say, but...
: Can you tell me the spaghetti story?
: You're ready for the spaghetti.
: Please never say that again.
: Sorry guys, but the spaghetti story is going to have to wait!
: What I just laid out in front of you will be your second main course for the night- and I'm sure it goes without saying, but it's better than stupid spaghetti.
: Spa-!
Sana’s eyes light up when a plate of omurice shows up in front of her.
Omurice is-
: Hm? Molly? What are you doing here?
: My hearthstone was off cooldown and I heard that Ami was making omurice, so I figured I'd drop by and pick some up!
: Here's a weebnote for you, Ayane- did you know that omurice is a Japanese comfort food made up of an omelette and, you guessed it- rice?
: ...Yeah. Yeah, I knew that.
: Did you also know that it’s a staple in not only many diners, but also places like maid cafes?
: Yup.
: Oh, hi Molly. I made an extra serving for you and put it in a container on the counter. You can just give it back to me in school, okay?
: Thanks, Ami! Grats in advance on completing your quest for your uncle's heart!
: Well, that was weird.
: This...
: This is...one of my favorite foods...
: My vote is for Ami.
: Huh? But you haven't even eaten it yet. How can cheap diner food like that beat homemade pasta?
: Ayane, I don’t think you understand.
: Ami’s been spending the last two months practicing this exact dish.
: I don’t know where her fascination with it came from, but I can assure you that she has all but perfected it.
: I’m...going to start eating now...
: Yeah...sorry, Ayane.
: You're going to lose this one.
As expected, Ami’s omurice is out of this world.
It’s kind of like eating a pillow if pillows were made of eggs and covered in ketchup.
Weird comparison, I know. But I promise you, there is nothing more comfortable than this very dish...
: I pick Ami.
: You know...maybe there is a god after all?
: I can’t...not vote for it...
: Even though it’s the same thing you picked...
: Why is this happening to me?
: Yay! This means I win round two!
: Don’t jump for joy just yet, Ami! We still have the dessert round!
: And I know exactly what these three need in order to finish this competition the right way!
: Ladies and gentlemen! Ayane-fans around the world!
: Feast your eyes on a timeless classic!
: You know it! I know it! We all know it!
: It’s-
: One very large banana!
: What the fuck is this?
: Okay, so...I was kind of hoping that I would beat Ami in the first two rounds so I didn’t have to worry about dessert.
: I’m...not really great at baking or...cooking any of that sweet stuff, so...
: The giant banana was really the only option.
: How?
: Why?
: I have so many questions.
: What...are we supposed to do with it?
: Eat it like any other banana!
: Peel it! Dice it! Share it with friends!
: Go bananas!
: I fucking hate you, Ayane.
: I don't think I want to eat this.
: Yeah...I don’t really trust it...
Ayane wound up having to drag the banana outside while Ami finished preparing her desserts...
: Okay! So, I decided to do something fun for the dessert round and made something special for all three of you!
: For Sana, an entire box of doughnuts! And for Sensei, some leftover ice cream we had in the freezer!
: It might not be much, but it still beats the giant banana! Ami wins!
: Oh. And for Maya-
: I can’t move.
: Is Maya...actually smiling right now?
: The easiest way to Maya's heart is with a watermelon. Remember that, Sensei.
: Ami, I can’t move. Help.
: She’s also easily paralyzed by excitement whenever someone surprises her with one!
: I can’t feel my legs.
: It’s actually kind of cute, isn't it? She's like one of those goats that faint whenever they get scared.
: Ami, help. Please.
: Feed it to me.
: Feed me the melon.
In the end, Ami was the clear winner of the first ever Arakawa vs Amamiya cookoff.
Would Ayane have had a chance if she had actually made a dessert? Maybe.
But I guess we’ll never know, will we?
There is still one thing on my mind, though.
And it’s something I just can’t seem to shake no matter how hard I try.
Just where the hell did Ayane find a banana that large?...
Ami’s affection has increased to [ami_love]!
Ayane’s affection has increased to [ayane_love]!
Sana’s affection has increased to [sana_love]!
Maya’s affection has increased to [maya_love]!
